title: Playing in the rain for soldiers who had waited for hours
summary: Soldiers sat on stumps in the rain since afternoon, so Holmes agreed to perform on their homemade stage.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And the Special Service Officer come and greeted everybody. "Oh, the boys are so happy to hear that you made

it here to the island." "Oh yeah." He says, "Do you know, they're waiting out there in the theatre for you now." And this was about four o'clock in the afternoon. He said, "They're waiting in the theatre, they're waiting now." Gee, in all that rain, we got to go through all that rain to get to the theatre? I just figured these soldiers are sitting in some big, beautiful theatre, high and dry and waiting for us to show up. No. I said, "It's raining out there. How are we going to make it to the theatre?" He said, "Oh, you'll make it to the theatre all right. We'll get you there." I said, "I don't get it. I don't see why they can't put it off for a day or so."

So anyway, we went to the theatre. Well, the theatre was nothing but a stage which the soldiers had built themselves. It wasn't bad, the stage wasn't bad. The only thing, the theatre part where the soldiers had to sit, that was nothing but out in the field, and they were sitting on tree stumps or boxes or anything, and had the raincoats and the things all over their head, and they been sitting there for hours waiting for our show to come on. So I looked out there, and I seen all these soldiers as far as I could see. Soldiers just sitting out there, covered up from the rain, waiting to see a show, like they're going to see something great.

So I said to the Special Service Officer, "Do you mean to tell me these soldiers have been sitting out here since four o'clock this afternoon?" He said, "Yes. Waiting to see your show." He said, "They deserve a show. They've been here so long," and this-that-and-the-other. I said, "Well, I was dead against it because of the weather, but if they've got nerve enough to sit out there in that rain, the way it is, and sit there four or five hours waiting to see a show, I'm not going to be the one to say no. I'm going to play part. Now, I don't have nothing to say about the rest of the band, but I'm glad to do my part. But they deserve it. They deserve everything they get."

So we did the show in the rain, and like I said, the stage wasn't bad. We were covered up. But they're the ones sitting out in the rain. Boy, oh boy. So we did the show, and oh boy, you'd have thought it was a big extravaganza we did. It went over like a ton of bricks, like it was really something great. They were applauding anything they seen out there.
